weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:start to seg3:end: a full-frame flat teal square holding '29400T' with no unit. Data stands still on its top edge. A tiny 'NASA's Cold Atom Lab (ISS)' label sits on the right edge. There is no motion for about 4s, and the narration is '5,000 light-years away, but NASA's freezer is 250 miles up'.
weakest_scene.root_cause: An area-proportional square was used for a distance comparison. The 5,000 ly vs 250 miles ratio is so large that the comparison partner shrinks to nothing, leaving one slab. '29400T' is a unit-less abbreviation that viewers cannot parse.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Draw the distance as a journey made of the subject. Earth with the ISS a hair above it, Data zooming a telescope/rocket out past the planets toward a far nebula, with the 250-mile hop visible as a tiny tick next to an enormous 5,000 light-year sweep. Use one readable headline ('5,000 light-years vs 250 miles') fully inside the frame. Data drives the zoom-out.
